discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (moire quantum matter)

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: 2D materials and van der Waals heterostructures
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that twisting two graphene layers to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees would make the electronic bands nearly flat, so that electron interactions would dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group built such devices with precise control of the twist angle. They found correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity that can be tuned by a gate voltage. This created a new field, moire quantum matter. One simple geometric parameter now gives access to strongly correlated phases, orbital magnetism, Chern insulators and, in related moire systems, the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect. The work stands out for its experimental rigour, its reproducibility across many laboratories worldwide, and the precise theoretical prediction that came before it. It has changed how condensed-matter physicists design and study interacting electron systems.
